title.narrative: Safe and Secure: Integrating Child Protection and WASH for Resilient Communities in Dhameer, Rural Damascus and as-Safira, Aleppo

description.narrative: ltpgtTerre des Hommes Foundation – Switzerland (Tdh) proposes a 12-month intervention to provide integrated Child Protection (CP) and WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene) assistance in the Dhameer and As-Safira subdistricts of Rural Damascus and Aleppo Governorates, respectively.ltbrgtTdh assessed the CP and WASH needs in these subdistricts, finding a high prevalence of CP risks, a lack of CP services, and insufficient access to water for domestic use. Addressing CP and WASH issues simultaneously is essential for several reasons: Article 24 of the Convention of the Rights of the Child highlights the child's right to health and the promotion of preventative health measures, which is significantly at risk without adequate water for domestic use. Moreover, a lack of water is incompatible with the child protection principle of the right to survival and development. At last, it leads to various child protection risks. These include diseases from unhealthy water, increased family violence due to stress and poor coping mechanisms, and adverse physical development as children are forced to help their families find water resources.ltbrgtThe findings of the needs assessment corroborate these links. Respondents mentioned aggressive communication, neglect, and both physical and emotional abuse of children by caregivers who face increasing pressure to provide for their families. Households are forced to find alternative solutions to cope with water scarcity, such as purchasing water at 40,000 SYP per cubic meter or collecting water from sources more than 500 meters away. Often, they rely on children for this task, which is time-consuming and leads to school absences. This reliance exposes them to health hazards from consuming water from unreliable sources. Extended displacement, poverty, lack of electricity, and worsening socio-economic conditions have led to children dropping out of school to help support their families financially. This places extra pressure on their caregivers, who struggle with the stress and anxiety of not being able to meet their families' basic needs.ltbrgtThe planned project will address these identified CP and WASH needs through a multisectoral intervention. The goal is to provide urgent CP services, including Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS), case management, and a positive parenting program, alongside water system repairs to enhance the well-being of children and their families. This includes ensuring adequate access to water in compliance with Ministry of Water Resource standards. Additionally, the project aims to build the capacity of communities and relevant stakeholders on Child Protection Minimum Standards, enabling them to identify and mitigate risks such as school dropouts, child labor, early marriage, and other challenges.ltbrgtThe project will reach 9,647 men, 14,469 women, 17892 boys, and 26,842 girls with life-saving humanitarian assistance. This will include MHPSS support for 1,500 children, a parenting care program for 750 caregivers, and specialized child protection services for 150 children through case management. The intervention will also improve access to water for domestic use for 68820 people in the targeted areas. Furthermore, it will increase the resilience of the affected communities by establishing community-based child protection committees (CBCPCs) and training them on Child Protection Minimum Standards (CPMS). These committees will then conduct awareness sessions on child protection within the communities. Tdh will also enhance and strengthen coordination within the CP Area of Responsibility (AoR) by facilitating an annual review and leading the development of the CP Awareness Harmonized Tool Kit in close coordination with the CP AoR Coordinator.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtlt/pgt
